style.vernacular: Former colonial capital of Burma on the Yangon river delta: a downtown grid of four-storey brick-and-stucco colonial mixed-use blocks (4.3 m ceilings, mezzanines) stained black-green by monsoon mould, surrounded by 6-8 storey walk-up apartment blocks in faded pastel paint with open balconies and rooftop water tanks, 1-2 storey detached houses in the satellite townships under corrugated zinc roofs, and gilded Buddhist stupas rising above leafy tree canopy. style.vernacular: Ancient walled Hausa city in the Sudano-Sahelian tubali tradition: ochre-brown mud-render (laterite-and-straw) compounds with flat roofs, horn-like corner pinnacles (zankwaye) and a decorated gatehouse (zaure) at each house; the old city is ringed by earth walls about 9 m high with gates (kofa); outside it, colonial Sabon Gari and Nassarawa have painted-sandcrete shophouses and bungalows, and the modern city is concrete and corrugated tin under neem and date palms on dusty laterite.
style.ornament: Hausa facade relief (zane) hand-carved in mud or cement render around the zaure and doors: interlaced knots (dagi), staff-of-office and sword motifs, geometric bands; horn-like corner pinnacles (zankwaye) and crenellated parapets on palace, gates and mosques; indigo-dyed cloth hung in the old city; hand-painted shop signs.
